claims.claim: AMC and Cinemark reported concession supplies at 18.1-18.9% of concession revenue in 2025 US filings.
claims.episode_span: Public filings show concession supplies running between eighteen and nineteen percent of concession revenue for AMC and Cinemark in 2025
claims.source_title: Cinema Concessions: Pricing, Stand Operations and Equipment
claims.supporting_quote: In 2025 Cinemark's US film rentals and advertising costs were 58.0% of admissions revenue, while its concession supplies were 18.9% of concession revenue. AMC's US food and beverage costs were 18.1% of food and beverage revenue the same year.

claims.claim: Popcorn costs theaters less than fifty cents per serving yet sells for eight dollars or more.
claims.episode_span: Popcorn kernels and flavored oil together fall below fifty cents per large serving in multiple industry benchmarks.
claims.source_title: Why Many Movie Theaters Make More Money On Snacks Than Tickets
claims.supporting_quote: It costs less than $0.50 to make a serving of popcorn, but when the movie theater staff scoop it into a bucket with a squirt of butter-flavored oil, it can come to you with as much as a 1,275% markup.

claims.claim: The 1948 Paramount decree ended studio ownership of theaters and led to theaters retaining roughly 40% of ticket revenue on average.
claims.episode_span: That split traces directly to the 1948 Paramount decree, which forced studios to divest their theater holdings and ended block booking.
claims.source_title: The United States v. Paramount and How Movie Theater Concessions Got So Expensive
claims.supporting_quote: In 1948, the Supreme Court ended the stranglehold Hollywood studios and distributors had on the U.S. movie market.
